summary.title: Databases in 2022: A Year in Review
summary.one_liner: A opinionated year-end recap of 2022 database news covering slowing VC funding, skepticism about blockchain databases, new DBMS launches like AlloyDB and Snowflake Unistore, and the loss of researcher Martin Kersten.
takeaways: Database venture funding slowed sharply in the second half of 2022 after large rounds earlier in the year.
The author argues blockchain databases offer no practical advantage over existing DBMSs outside cryptocurrency, and that QLDB is not a blockchain.
New systems such as Google AlloyDB, Snowflake Unistore, MySQL HeatWave, Meta's Velox, and InfluxDB IOx were announced or reached GA in 2022.
Reusable execution frameworks like Velox, DataFusion, and Polars may make OLAP DBMSs more similar over time.
Martin Kersten, a CWI researcher behind MonetDB and PRISMA/DB, died in July 2022.
summary.summary: This is Andy Pavlo's year-end retrospective on the database field for 2022, published on the OtterTune blog. It walks through the funding landscape (big rounds early in the year, a slowdown later), the author's view of blockchain databases, and a roundup of new DBMS announcements such as AlloyDB, Snowflake Unistore, MySQL HeatWave, Velox, and InfluxDB IOx. It also includes a memorial to Martin Kersten and a section on personal and company news. Much of the text is opinion marked "Andy's Take", and the last section is off-topic personal commentary, so readers should separate the factual reporting from the author's views.
